title: Latency Entropy Mosaic — heuristics, metric fences, and trace anchors
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a lightweight taxonomy and practical heuristics we can use when we design dashboards and tracing for latency-heavy inference flows. The guiding idea: treat latency signals as an "entropy mosaic" — many small noisy signals that together reveal structural problems if we fence, anchor, and slice them intentionally.

Audience:
Primarily SREs and runtime/serving engineers who own operator dashboards and incident playbooks; secondary: product/console team for rollout observability patterns.

High-level goals:
- Provide a small, opinionated set of metric fences (coarse->fine) that reduce noise and make investigation steps repeatable.
- Define trace anchor conventions to link dashboard panels to a tiny set of spans for fast session reconstruction.
- Suggest dashboard widgets and sampling rules tuned for tokenized LLM inference (kv-cache warmness, prefix hit-rate, generator tail latencies).
- Capture quick investigative recipes (first 6 steps) and low-cost probes to add during rollouts.

Core concepts (short):
- Entropy: variance in response time distributions especially at tail quantiles (95/99/99.9).
- Mosaic: tiled panels that together cover upstream, runtime, model, and network boundaries.
- Fences: coarse-grain aggregations that gate when to escalate to finer diagnostics (e.g., service-wide p95 rise -> tenant-level heatmap -> trace anchor).
- Anchors: minimal span metadata to reconstruct a session (request_id, route, model_variant, kv_warm_flag, node_id).

Metric fence proposal (3-tier):
- Tier 0 (Global health): service-level q50/q95/q99 request latency, request rate, error rate, capacity-utilization, cost-per-token estimate. Purpose: alerting and quick health.
- Tier 1 (Surface slices): per-route q50/q95/q99, per-model-variant p95, per-region p99, cache-hit-rate (kv prefix hits/requests). Purpose: triage which surface is affected.
- Tier 2 (Tenant/session): tenant or API-key heatmap for p95/p99, cold-start ratio, median kv-cache-warm-threshold, requests with fallback-model. Purpose: target investigation, paging.

Suggested metric definitions (wording to be used by instrumenters):
- request.latency_ms: wall-clock from ingress-receive to final-response-send (exclude streaming flush windows).
- request.backend_latency_ms: time spent in model-serving container from model-call-start to model-call-end (includes KV cache lookup).
- kv.prefix_hit_rate: cumulative ratio of requests served from prefix/KV cache within last 5m (numerator: prefix_hit; denominator: model_token_requests).
- generator.tail_tokens_ms: time to generate last N tokens (useful for sampling heavy-tail compute).
- session.kv_warm_index: heuristic score 0..1 computed from recent prefix_hits and session_length.
- route.fallback_rate: fraction of requests that fell back to lower-cost model in last 5m.

Trace anchor conventions (minimal set to include in spans/annotations):
- request-id (trace_id)
- route_name
- model_variant
- kv_cache_key_hash (truncated)
- kv_cache_hit boolean
- seq_len_estimate (tokens)
- node_id / instance_pool
- operator_stage annotation (ingest, routing, batch_wait, model_exec, postproc)

Sampling guidance (cost-aware):
- Baseline: always sample 1/1000 traces for end-to-end sessions to build longitudinal baselines.
- Alert-triggered burst: on Tier 0 or Tier 1 p99 threshold breach, increase sampling to 1/50 for the affected route/model for 10 minutes.
- KV-miss bias: preferentially sample traces where kv_cache_hit=false at 1/20 because cold starts are high-value for debugging.
- Tail-reservoir: maintain a small reservoir (500 traces/day) of high-latency (p99+) traces for offline analysis.

Dashboard mosaic layout (recommended tiles and drill paths):
- Row A: Global health fence (q50/q95/q99, total requests/min, error rate, compute utilization) — click -> show affected routes.
- Row B: Surface slices (per-route small multiples with p95 heatmap across regions; drop-down to select model variant).
- Row C: Cost and efficiency (tokens/second, cost-per-token estimate, batching efficiency, avg batch size).
- Row D: KV-cache and session warmth (kv.prefix_hit_rate trend, session.kv_warm_index distribution, cold start events).
- Row E: Anomaly probe timeline (synthetic probe latency, canary deviation, sampling notes).
- Drill path: From Row A p99 spike -> Row B identify route -> Row D check kv warmness -> Row E inspect sampled traces (trace anchors) -> fetch full trace/session.

Operator quick-play (first 6 actions):
1) Confirm global-signal: check Tier 0 panels and synthetic probes to rule out upstream infra incidents.
2) Isolate surface: open per-route p95 panel and sort by region/variant.
3) KV-check: look at kv.prefix_hit_rate; if drop observed, suspect cache invalidation or key-sharding regression.
4) Sampling jump: if no sampled traces exist, trigger alert-burst sampler for that route (1/50 for 10m).
5) Check rollout flags: verify canary traffic ratio, model_variant mapping, and any recent routing policy changes.
6) Escalate with minimal trace bundle: attach 3 p99 traces + heatmap snapshot + recent commit range.

Low-cost probes to add during rollouts (quick instrumentation):
- short-lived synthetic probe that replays representative prompt set every minute per-region and records kv-cache warm flag.
- sample-logger on model-serving entry that emits a compact JSON line with anchors only (no user PII).
- micro-benchmarks that run every 6h for each model_variant measuring generator.tail_tokens_ms for 50/100/200 token windows.

Naming and panel guardrails (to keep dashboards slim):
- Prefer 'route.model_variant.metric' naming for panels (e.g., "chat-complete.gptx-7b.request.p95_ms").
- Limit small-multiple axes to 12 items (otherwise switch to heatmap).
- Provide a one-line panel description with the investigation step (e.g., "If p99↑ -> open KV warmness panel and jump to traces").

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How sensitive should alert thresholds be to tenant-weighted usage? (we can use weighted p95 but cost is contention).
- Do we include streaming flush time in request.latency_ms? Current instrumentation inconsistent — proposal: separate streaming flush lag metric.
- Privacy: truncation strategy for kv_cache_key_hash to avoid leaking user data while preserving debugging value.

Next actions (short backlog):
- [Aisha] Draft metric instrument spec for request.latency_ms and backend_latency_ms (due 2024-10-17).
- [Marco] Implement trace-anchor compact logger PR (github PR link above) and add kv_miss bias sampling (due 2024-11-01).
- [Priya] Prototype mosaic dashboard in staging and capture drill-path clicks for 2 incidents (due 2024-11-15).
- [Omar] Run privacy review for kv key truncation and add redaction checklist (due 2024-11-05).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the dashboard 'mosaic' small — ergonomic for oncall. Heavy data exploration belongs in a separate troubleshooting workbook.
- When in doubt, add an anchor rather than a full payload to traces. This is low-cost and usually sufficient.

References and short links:
- playbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/OBS-entropy-mosaic
- sampling design notes: JIRA-OBS-3127
- related: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-playbooks#pr-59

End of sketch.

Comments welcome — this is intentionally terse and operational; will expand into instrument-spec and dashboard mock after alignment.
